title: STEP Fusion Programme Announces UK Manufacturing Partnerships with INFINITY, Manufacturing Technology Centre, and Kyoto Fusioneering
detail: At the start of UK Fusion Week, UK Fusion Energy (UKFE, the UK Atomic Energy Authority subsidiary delivering the STEP prototype tokamak) announced on September 17, 2026 a trio of partnerships to build out the manufacturing base for STEP. UKFE partnered with INFINITY, developer of a 200-acre advanced manufacturing site at Infinity Park in Derby, for prototyping, digital engineering, testing/validation and supply-chain collaboration using hot isostatic pressing, power-beam welding, and additive manufacturing for large, complex, high-integrity fusion components. Separately, UKFE became a Tier 1 member of the Manufacturing Technology Centre (MTC), opening a new R&D contract route through which UKFE expects to spend up to £10M accessing MTC and High Value Manufacturing Catapult expertise. Kyoto Fusioneering announced on the same day it will invest up to £3M to design and build a lithium oxide solid breeder blanket experiment with online tritium measurement, to advance STEP's tritium-breeding technology in coordination with Oak Ridge National Laboratory's UNITY-3 facility and General Atomics' Fusion Blanket Component Test Facility. UKFE Chief Commercial Officer Dan Bishop said delivering STEP 'will depend on manufacturing capabilities that do not yet exist at the scale we need.' STEP targets prototype construction in the 2030s with operations from 2040.

title: China National Nuclear Corporation Proposes International Fusion Engineering Cooperation Platform at IAEA General Conference
detail: At a side event of the 70th IAEA General Conference in Vienna ('Fusion for the Future: Engineering the Key Pathway to Realising Fusion Energy'), hosted by China Fusion Energy Co (CFEC, established 2025 and operator of the Southwestern Institute of Physics), the China National Nuclear Corporation (CNNC) proposed a new international cooperation platform to help move fusion energy from scientific research toward engineering applications, announced September 17, 2026. The event opened with the signing of a memorandum of cooperation on fusion engineering technologies between CFEC and the ITER Organization, plus a separate memorandum between CNNC's Southwestern Institute of Physics (SWIP) and Thailand's Institute of Nuclear Technology (TINT) for scientific research and exchanges. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) designates fusion energy a future priority industry, with SWIP's HL-3 tokamak having reached 'dual hundred-million-degree' operation (120M°C ion / 160M°C electron temperatures) in 2025; China's stated target is commercial fusion utilization by 2050.
